documents.title: CBDCs Are Not the Beast. Bad Architecture Is.
documents.subtitle: The life-giving ledger, SORA Nexus, and the constitutional design of digital money
documents.author: Makoto Takemiya
documents.html_summary: A SORA Contributor editorial on the constitutional design of digital money. It argues that the relevant question is how identity, visibility, rule-making, enforcement and appeal powers are separated and bounded.

sections.title: Architecture rather than label
sections.content: The essay argues that a CBDC is monetary infrastructure, and that risks arise from architecture, governance and limits on power rather than the acronym alone.

sections.title: Separated powers
sections.content: It distinguishes identity from transaction validity, issuance from retail service, compliance from omniscience, settlement from surveillance, and governance from arbitrary administration.

sections.title: Operational example
sections.content: It discusses Bakong’s two-tier structure as a model in which central infrastructure and customer-facing institutions retain distinct functions.

sections.title: Nexus context
sections.content: It connects shared settlement, data spaces, lanes, deterministic execution, canonical encoding, proofs and institutional messaging to bounded visibility and accountable intervention.

sections.title: Constitutional choice
sections.content: It contrasts refusal, managerial convenience and constitutional digital money, with explicit processes, constrained authority and auditable interventions.

documents.claim_scope: Attributed editorial source. The For Agents corpus indexes its architecture themes and preserves its source link; it does not restate it as protocol specification or policy.
